description: The terms somebody manages an investment account under: who the client is, who the advisor is, what they charge and how often, and when it started. A record rather than a PDF in a drawer because the fee is a recurring cost with compliance consequences — a fee disclosure that does not match what is actually being charged is the finding, and nobody can check that against a scan.
name: Advisory Agreement

fields.description: What this agreement is called, for a person reading the list.
fields.label: Agreement Name

fields.description: The managed account. Optional — an agreement can be signed before the account is opened — but where it is set it must belong to the same company, because a fee charged against one entity's account cannot be a cost of another's.
fields.label: Bank Account

fields.description: Active is the one in force. Superseded is what an amendment leaves behind — kept, never deleted, because the terms that were in force when a fee was charged are the terms that justify the fee.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The legal client, as the agreement names it — "Orchard Meadow, LLC". Free text rather than a Link to Company, deliberately: the signing entity on an agreement is frequently a trust or an individual that has no reason to exist in the chart of accounts.
fields.label: Client Entity

fields.description: The legal advisor, as the agreement names it.
fields.label: Advisor Entity

fields.description: The signed agreement in the governance register, where it has been filed there.
fields.label: Document Reference

fields.description: What the account is being managed FOR. It is the half of suitability that can be recorded; the other half is the client's circumstances, which do not belong in an accounting system.
fields.label: Objective

fields.description: Which of the two fee fields below is in force. Hybrid means both — a flat retainer plus a percentage — and is refused unless both are filled in, because a hybrid missing half of itself computes as whichever half survived.
fields.label: Fee Type
fields.options:
Percent of AUM
Flat Annual
Hybrid

fields.description: Annualised percentage of assets under management. 1.0 means 1%.
fields.label: Fee Percent of AUM

fields.description: How often the fee is actually billed. It is what turns an annualised rate into the number that will appear on a statement, and it is the one field that makes a computed fee comparable to a charged one.
fields.label: Billing Frequency

fields.description: When it ends. Empty means it has not — a Terminated agreement without one is refused, because "this ended" and "we do not know when" are different facts and only one of them can be billed against.
fields.label: Termination Date

fields.description: The agreement this one replaces. An amendment is a NEW record pointing back, and the old one becomes Superseded rather than being edited, so the terms in force on any past date are still readable.
fields.label: Amended From

fields.description: Why the terms changed. On an amendment this is the only place the reason is recorded — the prior record shows WHAT changed and says nothing about why.
fields.label: Amendment Reason
